clue.text: Work for kids — fair appeal for help by party

parts.note: fair as in just, even-handed
SOS is the distress signal
the Tories are the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A children's book is advertised alongside a political party's plea for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' simply places the party next to the rest. Kipling's collection of animal origin tales is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's collection of fables was written for children, so it is a literary work meant for kids.

clue.text: A couple of climbers in nursery, needing water, suffering damage

definitions.text: A couple of climbers in nursery, needing water, suffering damage

parts.words: A couple of climbers in nursery, needing water, suffering damage
parts.note: the nursery rhyme pair who went up a hill to fetch a pail of water, and one fell and broke his crown

explanation.surface: Two climbing plants in a garden nursery need watering and are getting damaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nursery' suggests a plant nursery and 'climbers' plants, but it is a nursery rhyme about two children climbing a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme tells of a boy and girl who climb a hill for water and then tumble down injured.

clue.text: Details for designer glasses

definitions.meaning: specifications, the technical details a designer works from

explanation.definitionFit: The short word is both an abbreviation of specifications and an informal word for spectacles.

clue.text: Rugby player has a lot of cider and a little beer

indicators.note: a lot of a word is most of it, so its final letters are dropped

parts.note: scrumpy is rough farmhouse cider from the West of England
a half is half a pint of beer

explanation.surface: A rugby player drinks plenty of cider and a small beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims PY off SCRUMPY to leave SCRUM.
explanation.definitionFit: The scrum-half is the rugby position that feeds the ball into the scrum.

clue.text: Remain valid, as a funny kind of act

definitions.meaning: an argument that holds up under scrutiny is said to do this
a comedian performing solo before an audience does this kind of comedy

explanation.definitionFit: To stand up is to hold good under examination; stand-up is solo comedy performed to an audience.

clue.text: Sound of brass instruments lacking a sexy quality

indicators.note: lacking says the following word is left out

parts.note: oompah is the rhythmic sound of a brass band

explanation.surface: A brass band's noise is said to lack sex appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: Oomph is informal for vitality or sex appeal.

clue.text: Closeness of two mines, exploding around cruiser's bow

indicators.note: around puts the shuffled letters on either side of the next piece
exploding blows the letters apart into a new order
two calls for the next word to be taken twice

parts.note: a single mine, here wanted twice over

indicators.note: a ship's bow is its front, so the first letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A warship comes close to a pair of mines blowing up round its prow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exploding' rearranges MINEMINE into IMMINENE, and 'around' wraps that round C, the bow of 'cruiser's', after IMMINEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Imminence is the state of being near at hand, closeness in time.

clue.text: British publication upsetting foreign characters

indicators.note: upsetting tips the word over, so in a down light it reads upwards

parts.note: nu is a Greek letter, so nus are characters of a foreign alphabet

explanation.surface: A British paper is accused of upsetting foreigners.
explanation.walkthrough: NUS read upwards gives the tabloid's name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sun is a British tabloid newspaper, a publication.

clue.text: A lot of sailors briefly in Mediterranean port

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: a ship's crew is a body of sailors

explanation.surface: Many sailors spend a short while in a Mediterranean harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A lot' looks like a unit of land, but A is taken alone and 'lot of sailors' is CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre (Akko) is an ancient port city on the Mediterranean coast of Israel.

clue.text: Behind chaps in wrestling area, preparing again for fight

parts.note: the rear is what is behind

indicators.note: in puts the chaps inside the wrestling area

parts.note: wrestlers grapple on a mat
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Men behind in a wrestling contest get ready for another bout.
explanation.definitionFit: Rearmament is equipping with weapons once more, readying for war.

clue.text: Children's writer Duke rescued

parts.note: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons

explanation.surface: A children's author is saved by a duke.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome is the English author of the Swallows and Amazons sailing books.
explanation.definitionFit: To ransom is to buy someone's release, so ransomed means freed or rescued.

clue.text: Does cutting-edge work with limited time, to be frank

parts.note: one who sharpens a blade hones it
time cut down to its abbreviation T

explanation.surface: Someone sharpens blades against the clock, to be candid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' is the verb hones, not the plural of doe.
explanation.definitionFit: Being honest means being truthful and candid, a synonym of frank.

clue.text: Lacking workers, as one may be after bad deal?

definitions.text: as one may be after bad deal?
definitions.meaning: a card player dealt too few cards would be left with a short hand

explanation.definitionFit: Short-handed means understaffed; read literally, a player with a short hand of cards after a misdeal.

clue.text: Gardener's fruit man still has since fall

definitions.meaning: Adam tended Eden, so the forbidden fruit was the first gardener's
the throat lump that legend says is a bit of the forbidden fruit stuck in Adam's throat after the Fall

explanation.definitionFit: The larynx bulge is named from the legend of the forbidden fruit lodging in Adam's throat.

clue.text: For this state, Maine's not going West

indicators.note: to go west is to be wrecked or die, so the letters are destroyed and rebuilt

parts.note: the state name with its S kept

explanation.surface: A New Englander says Maine is not heading west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going West' reads like a direction across the USA, but it is the idiom for being ruined, an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is a US state in the Upper Midwest.

clue.text: See why change, without a function, is cosmetic

indicators.note: without in the old sense of outside, so the shuffled letters go round the next pieces
change says the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a do is a party or social function

explanation.surface: A puzzled person asks why a cosmetic product changed, minus a feature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges SEEWHY into EYESHW; 'without' here means outside, so EYESH and W surround A and DO.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeshadow is a coloured make-up applied to the eyelids, a cosmetic.

clue.text: Nobody cut short when PM starts

indicators.note: cut short says the word loses its last letter

parts.note: nobody is no one

explanation.surface: No one is interrupted when the Prime Minister begins.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister but means post meridiem, afternoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Midday marks the start of the afternoon hours, labelled PM.

clue.text: Fellow in north

explanation.surface: A man living up in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a native of Finland is a fellow from the north of Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Finland, a Nordic country in Europe's far north, is a man of the north.

clue.text: Set out at night?

parts.note: a set of artificial teeth is taken out and left in a glass overnight

explanation.definitionFit: Dentures are a set of teeth commonly removed at bedtime.

clue.text: Allowed to chop up European plant for salad

parts.note: let means allowed

indicators.note: up reverses the word in a down light, reading it upwards

parts.note: to chop is to cut

explanation.surface: Someone is permitted to chop a European plant for a salad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is a link; 'up' turns CUT into TUC.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is a leafy plant grown chiefly as a salad vegetable.

clue.text: Warning about Black Prince

indicators.note: about places the warning around the next piece

parts.note: an alert is a warning
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An alarm sounds about the Black Prince, the medieval heir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Black Prince' looks like one name (Edward, son of Edward III), but Black is B and Prince the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's consort, a famous prince.

clue.text: What's wrong with English cake

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law

explanation.surface: Someone asks what is wrong with an English cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A torte is a rich layered cake of central European origin.

clue.text: European painter capturing surprised expression of Pacific islander

indicators.note: capturing holds the next piece inside the painter's name

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: An Old Master catches a startled look on an islander's face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European' fits the painter, not the islander: the Venetian master is the container, and the islander is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tahitian is a native of Tahiti, an island in French Polynesia in the Pacific.

clue.text: Bishop in row that divides Rome

indicators.note: in places the bishop within the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop in a dispute that splits the Roman church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' suggests a quarrel (rhymes with cow) but is a row of seats, a tier.
explanation.definitionFit: The river Tiber flows through Rome, splitting the city.

clue.text: Turn up at Twickenham, say, and thwart pack

definitions.meaning: attending a sports stadium such as Twickenham, England's rugby venue in London
a hunted fox does this by bolting into its earth, escaping the hounds

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to hide in a burrow, escaping hunting hounds; literally, visiting a stadium.

clue.text: Heavenly body it's not visible in round-the-world trip

indicators.note: the named word is missing from the longer word

parts.note: an orbit is one circuit of the globe

explanation.surface: A heavenly body cannot be seen during a voyage around the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is IT plus 'is'; IT vanishes from ORBIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An orb is a sphere, poetically a celestial body such as the sun or moon.

clue.text: Son with daughter included in organised group

indicators.note: included in places the daughter inside the son

parts.note: a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A son and daughter join a well-run organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Son' is not the usual S but BOY.
explanation.definitionFit: A body is a group of people organised for a purpose, as a governing body.

clue.text: Novel expression of delight from Miranda

definitions.meaning: in The Tempest Miranda exclaims 'O ...' on first seeing other people

explanation.definitionFit: Huxley took his novel's title from Miranda's delighted exclamation in Shakespeare's The Tempest.
